hook: Diederik Kingma studied in the Netherlands and completed a PhD at the University of Amsterdam in 2017, advised by Max Welling, focusing on deep learning and generative models. During his PhD, in 2013, he and Welling introduced the Variational Autoencoder, a generative model that combined neural networks with variational Bayesian inference and became one of the most widely used approaches for learning latent representations of data. The following year, working with Jimmy Ba, he published the Adam optimization algorithm, which quickly became the default method for training deep neural networks across nearly every area of machine learning. After finishing his doctorate, Kingma joined OpenAI as a founding member of its Algorithms team, then moved to Google Brain, where he continued developing generative modeling techniques including the Glow model and variational diffusion models. In 2024 he joined Anthropic to work on large scale machine learning.

quick_facts: PhD from the University of Amsterdam, 2017, advised by Max Welling
Co-created the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with Max Welling in 2013
Co-created the Adam optimizer with Jimmy Ba in 2014
Founding member of OpenAI's Algorithms team from 2015 to 2018
Received ICLR Test of Time Awards for both the VAE paper (2024) and the Adam paper (2025)

achievements.title: Variational Autoencoder (VAE)
achievements.impact: Introduced a generative model combining neural networks and variational Bayesian inference, giving researchers a practical way to learn compact latent representations of complex data, now foundational to generative AI.

achievements.title: Adam optimizer
achievements.impact: Created, with Jimmy Ba, the optimization algorithm that became the default choice for training neural networks across the field, thanks to its efficiency and robustness across a wide range of problems.

achievements.title: Generative modeling research at OpenAI and Google Brain
achievements.impact: Continued to advance generative modeling through work on the Glow normalizing flow model and variational diffusion models, extending the ideas behind the VAE into new model families.

achievements.title: Recognition for lasting impact
achievements.impact: Received consecutive ICLR Test of Time Awards, for the VAE paper in 2024 and the Adam paper in 2025, reflecting how central both works remain to modern machine learning.
